extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying 35 U.S.C. 102/102(b) (AIA) prior art rejections and exceptions (publications, patents, public use, on-sale, grace-period and inventor-originated exceptions) during examination of patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.08.aia — 102(a)(1) Activity Before the Effective Filing Date
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(1) the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph only in applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 where claims are examined under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103; must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.03.aia and 7.07.aia. Insert claim numbers in bracket 1. Provide full explanation/evidence for public use/on-sale/availability when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.12.aia — 102(a)(2) U.S. patent/application publication/WIPO publication naming another inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(2) the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under section 151, or in an application for patent published or deemed published under section 122(b), in which the patent or application, as the case may be, names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 where claims are examined under the AIA; must be preceded by 7.03.aia and 7.07.aia (and may be preceded by 7.08.aia). Only applies if the reference is (a) a U.S. patent under 151; (b) a U.S. patent application publication under 122(b); or (c) a WIPO publication of a PCT/international design application designating the U.S. with an earlier effective filing date. If such a document was published before the effective filing date of the claims, it is also applicable under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1). Include appropriate bracketed information (claim numbers, explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.14.aia — Pre-AIA 102(g) Priority of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: (g)(1) during the course of an interference another inventor establishes priority that before such person’s invention the invention was made by such other inventor and not abandoned, suppressed or concealed; (g)(2) before such person’s invention the invention was made in this country by another inventor who had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it. Consider conception, reduction to practice, and reasonable diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) is appropriate in an application/patent examined under the AIA only if the application/patent contains or contained a claim to an invention having an effective filing date (35 U.S.C.100(i)) before March 16, 2013 or a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) to a patent/application that contains such a claim. Must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.07.aia and 7.08.aia as appropriate, or by 7.103. Insert appropriate bracketed material (claim numbers, whether clearly anticipated/anticipated, prior art relied upon).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.15.01.aia — Provisional Rejection, 35 U.S.C.102(a)(2) (copending app with common assignee/applicant/joint inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application. The copending application would constitute prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if published under 122(b) or patented under 151; rejection is based on presumption of future publication or patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that subject matter in the copending application was obtained directly/indirectly from the inventor/joint inventor (102(b)(2)(A)); (2) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure (102(b)(2)(B)); or (3) a statement under 35 U.S.C.102(b)(2)(C) establishing common ownership/assignment/joint research agreement. Must be preceded by 7.07.aia. This rejection may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld). Insert bracketed info (claims, application no., common relationship, explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.15.aia — Rejection, 35 U.S.C.102(a)(1)/102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102 [2] as being [3] by [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 examined under AIA 102/103; must be preceded by 7.03.aia. Used to provisionally reject over a copending application that would be prior art under 102(a)(2) if published or patented; copending application must have common assignee, common applicant (35 U.S.C.118), or at least one common (joint) inventor. If claims would have been obvious over the copending application use form paragraph 7.21.01.aia. Insert bracketed material: claim numbers, application number, relationship label (assignee/applicant/joint inventor), and examiner’s explanation of anticipation. Note double-patenting/statutory vs nonstatutory double patenting guidance (form paragraphs 8.30–8.39) and requirement to precede by 7.06 when claiming priority to pre-March 16, 2013 applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.15.02.aia — Rejection, 35 U.S.C.102(a)(2) (common assignee/applicant/joint inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being [2] by [3]. The applied reference has a common [4] with the instant application and, based upon the earlier effectively filed date of the reference, constitutes prior art under 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection may be overcome by: (1) a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the reference's subject matter was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor (102(b)(2)(A)); (2) a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure (102(b)(2)(B)) if the same invention is not being claimed; or (3) a statement under 35 U.S.C.102(b)(2)(C) establishing common ownership/assignment/joint research agreement. Use only in AIA applications (filed on/after March 16, 2013) and must be preceded by 7.03.aia and 7.12.aia. If the reference issued/published before the effective filing date it also is applicable under 102(a)(1). Insert bracketed items (claim numbers, anticipated/clearly anticipated, prior art relied upon, common relationship). Address statutory double patenting (8.30–8.32) and nonstatutory double patenting (8.33–8.39) when relevant. Precedence by 7.06 required for priority to pre-March 16, 2013 filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.15.03.aia — Rejection, 35 U.S.C.102(a)(2) (no common assignee/inventor required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being [2] by [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reject over a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO patent application publication with an earlier prior art date under 102(a)(2) where the reference is not required to have a common assignee or inventor. Use only for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 examined under AIA 102/103 and precede with 7.03.aia and 7.12.aia as required. Insert bracketed items (claim numbers, anticipated/clearly anticipated with explanation, prior art).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.16.aia — Rejection, 35 U.S.C.102(a)(1) Public Use, On Sale, or Otherwise Publicly Available
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) based upon a public use or sale or other public availability of the invention. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 examined under the AIA; must be preceded by 7.03.aia and either 7.07.aia and 7.08.aia or by 7.103. Insert claim numbers in bracket 1 and provide a full explanation of the evidence establishing a public use/sale/other public availability in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.17.aia — 102(a)(1) Rejection Using Prior Art Excepted under 102(b)(2)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has provided evidence showing that the claimed invention and the subject matter disclosed in the prior art reference were owned by, or subject to obligation of assignment to, the same entity or were developed under a joint research agreement not later than the effective filing date. However, although reference [2] has been excepted as prior art under 102(a)(2), it is still applicable as prior art under 102(a)(1) that cannot be excepted under 102(b)(2)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may rely on the exception under 102(b)(1)(A) by showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the reference's subject matter was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor (and thus not prior art under 102(a)(1)), or rely on 102(b)(1)(B) by providing evidence of a prior public disclosure via affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(b). Use following form paragraphs 7.20.aia or 7.15.aia when anticipation is based on a reference excepted under 102(b)(2)(C) but still qualifying as prior art under 102(a)(1). Identify common assignee and the excepted reference in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.18.aia — Rejection, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C.102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) as being [2] by [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph only for an application or patent being examined under the AIA if it contains or contained a claim to an invention having an effective filing date (35 U.S.C.100(i)) before March 16, 2013 or a specific reference under 120, 121, or 365(c) to any patent/application that contains such a claim. Must be preceded by 7.14.aia or 7.103. Insert bracketed items (claim numbers, anticipated/clearly anticipated with explanation, prior art relied upon).

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C.102(b)(1)(A) — Grace Period Inventor-Originated Disclosure Exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure which would otherwise qualify as prior art under 102(a)(1) is not prior art if the disclosure was (1) one year or less before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; and (2) by the inventor or a joint inventor, or by another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a disclosure is inventor-originated requires case-by-case treatment depending on whether it is apparent from the disclosure itself or the application specification that it is inventor-originated. A disclosure is not prior art under 102(a)(1) if it: (1) was made one year or less before the effective filing date; (2) names the inventor or joint inventor as an author or inventor; and (3) does not name additional persons as authors on a printed publication or joint inventors on a patent. If the publication names additional authors/inventors beyond those in the application, it may not be apparent. Applicants may include a 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6) statement in the specification to identify grace period inventor-originated disclosures; the statement must convey the same information required in a 37 CFR 1.130(a) declaration. The Office provides a mechanism (affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130) to establish that a disclosure is not prior art due to a 102(b) exception. The one-year grace period is extended to the next business day if it would otherwise end on a weekend or federal holiday.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C.102(b)(1)(B) — Inventor-Originated Prior Public Disclosure Exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure which would otherwise qualify as prior art under 102(a)(1) is excepted as prior art if: (1) the disclosure was made one year or less before the effective filing date; and (2) the subject matter disclosed had been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor, a joint inventor, or another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception focuses on whether the 'subject matter' of the intervening disclosure had been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor/joint inventor (or someone who obtained it therefrom). There is no requirement that the mode of disclosure be the same; the previous disclosure need not be verbatim. However, the subject matter in the prior art relied upon must be the same 'subject matter' as previously publicly disclosed by the inventor — the exceptions do not apply if the only differences are insubstantial, trivial, or obvious. If an intervening disclosure includes both subject matter previously disclosed by the inventor and new subject matter, only the inventor-originated portions (e.g., A, B, C) are excepted; the new portions (e.g., D) remain prior art. Examples: species/genus distinctions — if inventor disclosed a species, a later publication of a genus that encompasses it may be excepted; converse may not. The exception's applicability is determined without comparing the subject matter to the claimed invention — it pertains to whether the intervening reference's subject matter had been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor. Applicants can establish applicability via affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 (see MPEP §2155.02/2155.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on 'apparent from the disclosure' test and applicant statements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a disclosure is inventor-originated may be apparent from the disclosure itself (e.g., the disclosure names the inventor/joint inventor and no additional persons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it is apparent from the disclosure that it is inventor-originated (names the inventor/joint inventor and lacks additional authors/joint inventors), Office personnel may not apply the disclosure as prior art under 102(a)(1). If not apparent, applicant may use 37 CFR 1.130 affidavits/declarations to establish the exception. Applicants may include a statement in the specification under 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6) identifying grace period inventor-originated disclosures to expedite examination; that statement should convey the same information as a 1.130(a) declaration and applicants should provide copies of the disclosures where appropriate. Adding such a statement after filing may be considered new matter; use 37 CFR 1.130(a) to submit after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and procedural mechanism to establish 102(b) exceptions (37 CFR 1.130 affidavits/declarations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office has provided a mechanism for filing an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 to establish that a disclosure is not prior art due to an exception in 102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inventor-originated status is not apparent from the disclosure, applicants may establish applicability of 102(b)(1)(A)/(B) by affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(a)/(b). MPEP §217 and §2155 discuss using affidavits/declarations to show that a disclosure was inventor-originated or that subject matter had been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor (or obtained from them). If specification as filed contains a specific reference to a grace period disclosure and an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 is of record, the Office may consider the disclosure apparent as inventor-originated, provided explanation and no contrary evidence exist.
